summary.headline: Biocon Q4 FY26 operating revenue up 10% YoY ex-lenalidomide to biosimilars-led growth; EBITDA Rs1,073 crore at 23% margin.
summary.overview: Biocon reported Q4 FY26 operating revenue growth of 10% YoY excluding the one-time generic lenalidomide benefit in Q4 FY25, led by biosimilars (+12%) and generics ex-lenalidomide (+13%), with CRDMO up 2%. Group EBITDA was Rs1,073 crore at a 23% margin, up 29% YoY on a like-for-like basis, and reported net profit before exceptionals was Rs179 crore. Management said the biosimilars and generics integration was completed in under 100 days and the major capex phase is substantially complete, shifting focus to utilisation, margins and deleveraging. Net debt has fallen to about $1.1 billion from more than $1.5 billion in March 2025, and interest cost savings of about Rs70-75 crore per quarter are now in the P&L.

segments.name: Biosimilars
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs2,756 crore (+12% YoY, about +7% in USD), EBITDA Rs720 crore at 26% margin (+33% YoY); R&D at 7% of revenue. FY26 revenue and EBITDA grew 16% and 40% like-for-like.

segments.name: Generics
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs847 crore, +13% YoY ex-lenalidomide, driven by generic liraglutide in Europe; EBITDA Rs75 crore at about 8% margin. FY26 ex-lenalidomide revenue +17%, EBITDA +73%.

segments.name: CRDMO (Syngene)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs1,037 crore (+2% YoY, +13% QoQ), hit by a single large molecule biologics client; 14 audits in quarter, 85 for FY26; obtained GCP NABL accreditation.

guidance_outlook: No numeric guidance given for FY27 biosimilars revenue; management said ramp-up from new launches is expected mainly in the second half of FY27.
Generics: focus on margin improvement as newer assets stabilise and utilisation improves; GLP-1 revenue (under 10% of FY26 business) expected to scale.
Currency tailwind expected in H1 FY27 for biosimilars; budget for incremental growth from launches mainly in H2.
Interest savings of about Rs300 crore annualised, full benefit visible from FY27.
Net debt expected to stay at $1.1-1.2 billion subject to working capital; free cash flow to go to debt reduction.
Syngene: focus on execution and more stable performance after FY26 challenges.
Management expects some ASP erosion in North America to be budgeted, but has seen limited erosion so far.
capex_capacity: Malaysia: drug product capacity doubled with Line 2 being qualified and expected operational soon; drug substance doubling expected towards end of FY27.
Bangalore: only minor debottlenecking expected; management sees no need for large greenfield capex.
Biosimilar capacity utilisation described as healthy but not quantified; some human insulin supported by CMOs.
Generics: state-of-the-art facilities now on stream, with peptide fermentation and drug product fungibility; margin improvement depends on utilisation.
Capital allocation: major investment phase described as substantially complete; no large-ticket greenfield expansion planned.
demand_pricing: Geographic mix for biosimilars: North America about 40%, Europe and ANZ about 35%, emerging markets about 25% long term; North America slightly higher in the last two quarters, about 46% of biosimilars this quarter.
Ustekinumab (Yesintek) reportedly close to a fifth of the US market per IQVIA data as of February, with favourable formulary placements.
Oncology biosimilar market share steady at about 23-25%; insulin glargine market share about 11%.
Product scale: insulin franchise above $300 million, adalimumab above $250 million, pegfilgrastim and trastuzumab around $200 million, bevacizumab above $100 million (ex-US).
Insulin total addressable market cited at about $7-8 billion, of which recombinant human insulin about $1.5 billion; limited players and Chinese approvals seen as validating the market.
FDA draft guidance removing Phase III requirement is seen as cutting development cost by about 50% and timelines by 3-4 years; management views it as advantageous to Biocon.
Management prioritises profitable growth over market share in US medical benefit products, citing ASP erosion risk.

qa_highlights.question: How should FY27-FY28 biosimilar revenue and the Q4 FY27 exit run rate be thought about after the Q3 slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a sequential rise from about $279-280 million in Q3 to about $300-plus million in Q4 (about 12% rupee growth) and stable full-year margins; it declined to give numeric guidance and pointed to H2 FY27 ramp-up from launches including Yesintek and Aspart.

qa_highlights.question: How will free cash flow be used in FY27 given the merger with Biocon Biologics?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Kedar Upadhye said all free cash goes first to net debt reduction, with net debt about $1.1 billion and expected to stay at $1.1-1.2 billion subject to working capital; interest cost savings are about Rs70-75 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of biosimilar sales and the largest products?
qa_highlights.answer: North America about 40%, Europe and ANZ about 35%, emerging markets about 25% long term; North America about 46% of biosimilars this quarter. Insulin above $300 million globally, adalimumab above $250 million.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for aflibercept (Yesafili) and Aspart (Kirsty) in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Yesafili US launch is planned for H2 FY27 under a negotiated settlement date; terms are confidential. Aspart commercial play in the US planned for H2 FY27 after closed-door network share, with ramp expected from H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation and is further capacity needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation described as healthy but not quantified; with Malaysia DP and DS doubling and external CMOs, management sees no need for large greenfield capex, only minor Bangalore debottlenecking.

qa_highlights.question: How will generics margins scale and what is the gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin in the early 40s, split about two-thirds API and one-third generics; Q4 generics EBITDA margin under 10% with operating leverage and product mix; margin focus expected in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of FDA draft guidance on biosimilar development on incumbents?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no incremental challenge to existing products, citing strong positions and CMC and analytical comparability capabilities; views the change as an advantage for Biocon.

risks_watch: Biosimilar revenue ramp depends on H2 FY27 launches (Yesafili, Aspart, denosumab in US); no numeric guidance given.
ASP erosion in US medical benefit products and possible aggressive share gains by competitors (e.g., aflibercept earlier entrant).
Syngene dependence on a single large biologics client; FY26 challenges to continue into FY27.
Generics margins still around 8% EBITDA; improvement contingent on utilisation of new facilities.
Chinese insulin approvals could add competition in insulin and RHI markets.
Callable USD bonds (6.67% coupon) from October 2026 at call premium; decision on early redemption pending.
Q4 OCI item of about Rs760 crore reclassifiable and Rs210 crore non-reclassifiable raised by an analyst was deferred to offline discussion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on biosimilar launches, balance sheet and operating leverage, but deliberately non-committal on quarterly and FY27 numbers, repeatedly steering to a broader time window. Evasive on Yesafili settlement terms and on the OCI reconciliation, which was deferred offline.
key_quotes: So, we are quite bullish about how our products are shaping up.
We're not looking at very big-ticket greenfield kind of expansion because we don't need it to support the business plan that's going forward.
Every dollar that we generate out of free cash, the first claim is going to be to reduce debt, and we are pretty serious about it.
This is not a quarter-on-quarter conversation. Look at it on a broader window.
